Backswing Ventures Announces Investment in Ukrainian Defense Technology Company Vigilant Works
News provided by
Backswing Ventures
Nov 12, 2026, 08:30 ET
Share this article
Share this article
ORLANDO, Fla. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Backswing Ventures, the defense venture capital firm, today announced its investment in Vigilant Works , a Ukrainian defense technology company developing autonomous counter-unmanned aerial systems (C-UAS), high-speed interceptor platforms, and radar-based detection capabilities designed to address increasingly sophisticated aerial threats.
Continue Reading
Backswing Ventures logo
The investment will support Vigilant Works' continued development of its autonomous guidance technologies, next-generation radar capabilities, and expansion of its operations as the company prepares to scale production and establish a broader presence across NATO-allied countries.
Backswing Ventures invests selectively in companies addressing critical challenges across defense and national security. As aerial threats continue to evolve in speed, sophistication, and scale, the ability to detect, track, and intercept them autonomously is becoming increasingly important. Vigilant Works is developing an integrated approach to counter-UAS operations, combining high-speed interception, autonomous guidance, and radar technology into a scalable defense ecosystem.
Founded by a team of engineers and defense technology entrepreneurs, Vigilant Works is developing an autonomous counter-UAS ecosystem combining interceptor platforms, proprietary autonomy technologies, and radar-based detection capabilities. Its first-generation Algiz-1 has undergone battlefield testing, providing operational experience that informs the development of its next-generation systems. The company is currently advancing Algiz-2, a next-generation interceptor capable of speeds exceeding 600 km/h and designed to address increasingly sophisticated aerial threats.
Vigilant Works has recently entered active battlefield testing of Algiz-2 and secured its first commercial agreements outside Ukraine. The company is also developing its proprietary autonomy stack and radar solutions in Ukraine, with investment capital supporting continued technology development and preparations to scale production and operations across NATO-allied countries. The company is a member of Brave1, Ukraine's defense technology coordination platform, and was previously selected for the Brave1 / Ministry of Defence EU4UA program.
"We are excited to support Vigilant Works as they continue developing and scaling their autonomous defense capabilities," said Kyle Asman , Managing Partner at Backswing Ventures. "The evolution of aerial threats is creating an increasingly urgent need for effective counter-UAS solutions. Vigilant Works has the benefit of developing its technology in an environment where these capabilities are being tested against real operational requirements. We believe the team's focus on autonomous interception, radar, and high-speed threats addresses an important and growing need across the defense ecosystem."
"We believe the next leap in counter-UAS will come from rethinking the entire interception chain, much like rocketry did decades ago. Detection, radar, autonomy, and high-speed interception cannot be developed in isolation. Erie Strategic Ventures: Investments In Blitzy And HiddenLayer To Advance Enterprise AI Infrastructure And Security
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 12, 2026
Erie Strategic Ventures: Investments In Blitzy And HiddenLayer To Advance Enterprise AI Infrastructure And Security
Erie Strategic Ventures, the corporate venture capital arm of Erie Insurance, has announced investments in Blitzy and HiddenLayer, two technology companies focused on enterprise AI infrastructure, software modernization, and artificial intelligence security. The investments expand Erie Strategic Ventures’ portfolio of companies developing technologies that can help organizations deploy, manage, and secure AI applications.
Blitzy provides an autonomous software development platform designed to modernize large enterprise codebases through coordinated AI agents. HiddenLayer develops security technology that protects generative, predictive, and agentic AI systems throughout their lifecycles.
The investments reflect Erie Insurance’s continued exploration of AI technologies that could support its operations, independent insurance agents, and policyholders.
Erie Strategic Ventures was launched in August 2022 to invest in companies operating across the personal and commercial insurance value chain, as well as adjacent technology markets.
The venture capital program is operated with support from Cerity Partners Ventures, which helps corporations manage strategic investment initiatives.
Through the program, Erie Insurance combines capital investment with opportunities for technology collaboration and business development.
Blitzy Focuses On Autonomous Software Development
Blitzy develops an AI-powered software engineering platform intended to help enterprises modernize legacy systems and accelerate new application development.
The company’s technology uses a proprietary ontology and graph-based architecture to develop a detailed understanding of large software codebases.
This approach is designed to provide AI systems with contextual information about how applications, components, and dependencies interact.
Using that information, Blitzy coordinates thousands of AI agents operating in parallel to perform software development tasks.
The platform is intended to address challenges associated with maintaining and updating complex enterprise software environments.
Large organizations frequently operate systems that have accumulated years of modifications, integrations, and dependencies.
Modernizing these environments can require significant engineering resources because changes to one component may affect other applications or business processes.
Blitzy’s approach seeks to improve efficiency by enabling AI agents to analyze software architecture and coordinate development activities.
The company also supports the creation of new software products, allowing engineering teams to use autonomous agents for development workflows.
For insurance companies and other financial services organizations, software modernization can be particularly important because many essential business processes depend on established technology systems.
Erie Strategic Ventures’ investment provides exposure to technology intended to improve enterprise software development and infrastructure management.
